scope: Theorem 7.16 (Spacetime Penrose inequality for complete initial data) of the manuscript “The spacetime Penrose inequality and enclosing area” (preprints/The-spacetime-Penrose-inequality-and-enclosing-area-September-27-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 260 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 9bb0c350914915db), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 81. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let (M, g, K) be a connected orientable smooth three-dimensional initial data set without boundary, with g complete. Suppose that outside a compact set M has finitely many asymptotically flat ends. On each end, in its asymptotic coordinates, assume g − δ = O2(r−q ), K = O1(r−1−q ), q > 1 2, and finite ADM energy and momentum limits with the normalizations (7.4)–(7.5). The decay exponents may differ between ends. Assume that the physical constraint densities (7.1) obey µ ≥ |J|g and that both µ and |J|g are integrable on M. For every chosen end and every admissible boundary S in Definition 7.15, its ADM vector (E, P) satisfies E > |P|δ, √︂ E2 − |P|2 δ ≥ √︄ Amin(S) 16π . (7.37)
